newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber buoyed by Chinese inquiries.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber buoyed by Chinese inquiries.

text.p: The Singapore rubber market was boosted at the close on Monday by Chinese buyers said to be making inquiries in the market and modest shortcovering for RSS3 and TSR20 rubber, dealers said.
"The Chinese have been asking for RSS3 and TSR20 but I don't know if anything has been finalised yet. The Chinese were checking prices and they may do this for quite some time," a trader said.
"They're (the Chinese) making inquiries and they've been doing so most of the day. They're looking mostly at RSS3 grade rubber," another trader said.
Traders said the market was also devoid of players as most dealers in the Singapore market were attending an industry seminar in Indonesia.
"Nobody wants to do anything and there are only a few people around at the moment," a dealer said.
At around 0945 GMT, September RSS3 was seen at 89.50-91.50 U.S. cents a kg from 89.25 cents.

September RSS1 was seen at 134.25 Singapore cents (93 U.S. cents) a kg from the previous 133.25 cents. September TSR20 was seen steady at 131.00 Singapore cents (91 U.S. cents) a kg. - (US$1 = S$1.43) - Rene Pastor (65-870-3305)
